niche: Psychology & human behavior (biases, habits, social dynamics)

ideas.title: Why Favors Make Friends
ideas.angle: It reveals the counter-intuitive truth that asking someone for a small favor actually makes them like you more, rather than doing a favor for them.

hook.en: Ask for a favor to be liked.
hook.fr: Demande un service pour être aimé.

ideas.reason: Social hack videos are currently viral on TikTok and Shorts because they offer immediate 'cheat codes' for social life. The Ben Franklin effect is a classic curiosity gap topic.
sources: Jecker, J., & Landy, D. (1969). Liking a Person as a Function of Doing Him a Favour.

ideas.title: Why Your Flaws Are Attractive
ideas.angle: It explains the Pratfall Effect: how highly competent people become significantly more likable and relatable when they make a small mistake or show a flaw.

hook.en: Your mistakes make you more likable.
hook.fr: Tes erreurs te rendent plus apprécié.

ideas.reason: Relatable content regarding social anxiety and the pressure to be perfect performs well. This provides 'relief' to the viewer, encouraging shares and saves.
sources: Aronson, E., Willerman, B., & Floyd, J. (1966). The effect of a pratfall on increasing interpersonal attractiveness.

ideas.title: Why You Overvalue Your Work
ideas.angle: It breaks down why we feel a stronger emotional bond and higher perceived value for things we had a hand in creating, even if they are objectively low quality.

hook.en: You love it because you built it.
hook.fr: Tu l'aimes car tu l'as construit.

ideas.reason: The 'IKEA effect' is a trending search term in behavioral economics. It explains common household arguments and consumer habits, making it highly relatable for a general audience.
sources: Norton, M. I., Mochon, D., & Ariely, D. (2012). The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love.
